title: Under-Sink Organization Ideas for the Cabinet Everyone Avoids
description: Under-sink organization ideas for kitchens and bathrooms: a 4-step plan to tame the pipes and 7 Amazon finds that fit around them.
intro:
Every home has one: the cabinet under the sink. It holds seventeen half-empty spray bottles, a sponge from 2022, a mystery bag of more bags and a drip tray you're scared to look at.

Under-sink cabinets are hard to organize because of the pipes, the depth and the fact that we open them in a hurry, grab something and slam the door.

But this is also one of the most satisfying spaces to fix, because a little effort makes a huge difference every single day. Here's the plan.

sections.heading: Step 1: Empty it and check for leaks
sections.body:
Set a timer for 15 minutes and pull everything out. While it's empty, take a quick look for drips or water damage. Catching a small leak now saves a big headache later.

Wipe the base. If it's stained or worn, a cheap shelf liner makes it feel fresh and easier to wipe next time.

sections.heading: Step 2: Edit ruthlessly
sections.body:
Look at what came out:

- Combine duplicates (two half bottles of the same spray become one).
- Toss things that are empty, dried out or broken.
- Pass along cleaners you never use.
- Take the extra bags out. Keep a reasonable stash. You know which drawer has more.

Most people lose half of what was under the sink in this step.

sections.heading: Step 3: Work around the pipes
sections.body:
The pipes are the whole problem, so organize around them:

- **Two-tier pull-out organizers** fit on either side of the pipe and slide out like drawers.
- **Stackable clear drawers** give you rows instead of a heap.
- **Door-mounted organizers** hold sponges, gloves or a small trash bag roll on the inside of the door.
- **A tension rod** across the top holds spray bottles by their triggers.

Measure the space around the pipe before you buy anything. Width, depth and height clearance.

sections.heading: Step 4: Group and label
sections.body:
Put like with like:

- **Kitchen:** dish soap and dishwasher stuff, cleaning sprays, trash bags, sponges.
- **Bathroom:** backup toiletries, cleaning stuff, hair care, first aid.

Label each drawer or bin. Future-you, reaching under the sink with wet hands, will appreciate knowing exactly where to grab.

sections.heading: Keep a 'grab and go' kit
sections.body:
In the bathroom, keep a small cleaning kit right under the sink: toilet cleaner, a spray, a cloth and wipes. When you notice something's grimy, you can clean it on the spot without walking to the kitchen.

This one small change makes bathroom cleaning happen way more often, because there's no trip to get supplies (and get distracted on the way).

sections.heading: Safety note for little ones
sections.body: If you have small kids or pets, add a cabinet lock and move harsh cleaners up high. Organized and safe can live together.

sections.heading: The 30-second monthly check
sections.body: On the first of the month, open the cabinet, glance around and toss anything empty. That's it. Thirty seconds keeps it from sliding back into the black hole.

outro:
Fifteen minutes, one cabinet and a couple of organizers that fit around the pipes. It's one of the fastest wins in the house.
